message.content:
Here are a few popular sushi spots you might want to try in Tokyo:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights |
|------------|----------|------------|
| **Sushi Saito** | Ginza | Michelin‑starred, intimate 10‑seat setting; known for meticulous preparation and seasonal ingredients. |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza | 2 Michelin stars; offers a refined omakase experience with a focus on subtle flavors. |
| **Sushi Jiro (Jiro Sushi)** | Roppongi | Famous from *Jiro Dreams of Sushi*; 3 Michelin stars; very high demand and reservation‑only. |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Popular for fresh fish straight from the market; long lines but worth it for the quality. |
| **Sushi Zanmai** | Multiple locations | Casual chain with a wide selection of rolls and nigiri; open 24/7 at many branches. |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | Classic sushi experience with a reputation for excellent service and high‑quality fish. |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Shinjuku | Known for its creative rolls and friendly atmosphere; great for both locals and tourists. |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Ebisu | Small, family‑run shop offering a relaxed vibe and fresh, affordable sushi. |

If you’re planning a visit, it’s a good idea to make reservations ahead of time—especially for the Michelin‑starred places—and consider the seasonality of the fish when choosing your dining window. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
